subject: ventures/jobshop-quote
auditor: agent session (Claude), quality round 108, see run record
professional: an experienced CNC / fabrication job-shop estimator; they check first that machine-hour rate x cycle time and setup-once-per-lot are right at every quantity break, that material is blank size x density x $/lb plus a drop/kerf allowance (or whole bars), that outside processing carries its lot minimum and its own markup, that markup is not confused with margin, and that a missing input blocks the quote instead of being guessed

evidence.correctness: Three quotes (seven quantity breaks) worked by hand from first principles and compared to computeCost output from a script the auditor wrote (node --experimental-strip-types probe.mts private-monorepo/apps/jobshop-quote/src/shared/costing.ts): all 7 unit prices and totals match to the cent, including per-lb plate with a material minimum and an outside-service lot minimum (A), round bar with a separate setup rate, in-house finishing, a lot extra and a binding line minimum (B), and per-stock bar bought in whole pieces with two ops on one machine (C). Blocking: no blank, no density, no parts-per-stock, no material, a machine id not on this card and duplicate breaks each return an issue and no price. One wrong-by-omission output: an operation with 0 setup and 0 cycle minutes prices without an issue (cost = material only), and the client turns a blank minutes field into 0 (quote-detail.tsx:379) and starts every new operation at 0 cycle minutes (quote-detail.tsx:665).
evidence.completeness: README/ROADMAP 'Done' items checked by running the suites: costing engine, extraction verification, cover note, PDF page count, rate-card and settings import, CAD suggestions (rough, cut, bend, drill with feed and pecks, tap), routings, repeat parts, quote diff, win/loss: pnpm test:unit 31 files / 421 tests pass; pnpm test:worker (API end to end in workerd, incl. cross-tenant isolation) 34 files / 217 tests pass. Deploy and live billing are listed under Next (item 3), not claimed done. Not run: pnpm test:e2e (browser). No stubs or TODOs found in costing.ts.
evidence.verification: pnpm test:unit: 421 pass, 0 fail (2.8 s). Eight hand-seeded mutants in costing.ts, each run against src/shared/costing.test.ts and reverted (private repo status clean afterwards): finishing lot minimum dropped, in-house finishing taken out of labor markup, scrap halved, material minimum dropped, setup rate ignored, material-not-chosen gate inverted, extras at labor markup - all 7 CAUGHT; unit price Math.ceil -> Math.round SURVIVED (no test has a total that is not a multiple of the quantity). The main pricing test is hand-checked in its comments; the author's tests are strong but the zero-minute operation case is untested because the engine does not treat it as an issue.
evidence.craft: Read src/shared/costing.ts (944 lines), costing.test.ts (test names), src/client/routes/quote-detail.tsx (operation editor), src/shared/api.ts (rate schemas). Engine is pure, zod-validated, integer cents with one rounding per component, a basis line per component and a rate snapshot; issue checks run before any arithmetic so the later '?? 0' fallbacks are unreachable. Concerns: costing.ts mixes the pricing engine with ~500 lines of CAD suggestion helpers; computeCost throws a ZodError on invalid input instead of returning issues (callers validate first); client num('') -> 0 is a silent fallback into a pricing input.
evidence.claims: Public front door: ventures/machine-shop-guides pages and platform/pages/industry-manufacturing.mjs call the product 'In development (early access)', 'Neither is released yet', 'Pricing is not set yet' - backed (ROADMAP item 3: not deployed; checkout dark). 'Prices from your own shop rates, setup times and material costs' - backed by computeCost (pure function of card and inputs) and the unknown_* issues. 'Keeps every quote and its assumptions' - backed by the rate snapshot and basis lines. 'Reads an RFQ (the email, the drawings, the CAD)' - drawings are read as converted text; reading title blocks from page images is still open (flagships.yaml item 3), so slightly generous. ventures/cnc-machining-quote-calculator makes no claim about the paid product. ARCHITECTURE rule 2 'Missing data blocks pricing; it is never guessed' lists its cases accurately, but a blank cycle-time field priced as 0 sits against its spirit. portfolio/flagships.yaml 'next' still lists the DXF sheet-metal path as open though ROADMAP item 5 records it done 2026-11-25 (stale).
evidence.fitness: Walked an estimator's job through the engine: rate card, three typical parts, quantity breaks 1-100, outside anodize and passivate, material certs, line minimum - the price table is what an estimator would produce by hand. Gaps hit in the first hour on a production quote: no scrap/yield starts (to ship 100 at 3% fallout you start 104; machine time, outside processing and per-stock material are all priced on the shipped quantity); programming, first-article and inspection have no per-lot labor line (setup minutes or a lot extra marked up at the material rate are the workarounds); parts per bar is typed by hand rather than derived from bar length, part length, kerf and grip (the free calculator does both). And no shop can use it today: the app is not deployed (ROADMAP item 3).
evidence.domain: Compared with standard job-shop estimating practice (machine/labor rate x hours, setup once per lot, material by weight or whole stock units with a drop allowance, outside processing with vendor lot minimums and its own markup, quantity breaks recomputed per lot) the method is right: setup and lot minimums amortise correctly, outside services carry their own markup, per-stock material buys whole pieces, and the settings import refuses 'Margin' with 'a 20% margin is a 25% markup'. Departures: kerf/facing/drop only as a percent of blank weight, not a per-cut length allowance; no part-scrap/yield starts; zero-minute operations accepted. A senior estimator would sign off on the core with those limits stated, which the README does not yet state.

defects.what: An operation with 0 setup and 0 cycle minutes prices without an issue, and the quote editor sends 0 for a blank minutes field and starts every new operation at 0 cycle minutes, so an unfilled cycle time can reach a sent quote as free machine time (the line minimum may hide it). ARCHITECTURE rule 2 says missing data blocks pricing.

No scrap/yield starts: every break prices machine time, outside processing and per-stock bars on the shipped quantity; fallout exists only as a % of blank weight. The free front-door calculator models starts = ceil(good / (1 - fallout)); the paid engine does not.

No per-lot labor line for programming, first-article or inspection: the workarounds are setup minutes or a lot extra, and extras are marked up at the material rate, so shop labor entered that way is marked up as a purchased item.
Unit-price rounding is untested: Math.ceil -> Math.round survives costing.test.ts, which would let unit x quantity fall below the computed price by up to q/2 cents.
Parts per stock piece is typed by hand; there is no bar-yield calculation from bar length, part length, parting kerf and grip/remnant, and kerf/drop on per-lb material is only a weight percentage.

Manufacturing page says the product 'Reads an RFQ (the email, the drawings, the CAD)'; drawings are read as converted text only, and reading title blocks from page images is still open (flagships.yaml next item 3).
flagships.yaml 'next' for jobshop-quote still lists the DXF sheet-metal path as open; ROADMAP item 5 records cut, bend and sheet-blank suggestions done 2026-11-25.

verdict: Meets the bar (correctness 3, claims 3, verification 3, median 3); finished (completeness 3). The costing engine is exact: three quotes (seven breaks) worked by hand from a typical rate card match its output to the cent, setup and lot minimums amortise correctly over quantity, outside services carry their own markup, per-stock bars are bought whole, markup is never confused with margin, and six kinds of missing input block the price. Tests are strong (421 unit, 217 worker, all pass; 7 of 8 seeded mutants caught, the survivor being unit-price rounding). The worst defect is that a blank cycle time becomes 0 and prices as free machine time instead of blocking, against the app's own 'missing data blocks pricing' rule. Fitness is 2: the app is not deployed, and an estimator quoting a production lot will miss scrap/yield starts and a per-lot programming/FAI line, both of which the free front-door calculator already models.
